name: CA-44
label: Safe D

model.rationale: A heavily Democratic incumbent seat paired with a roughly fifty-to-one fundraising gap leaves Angel without the resources to compete; with no polling or expert ratings suggesting vulnerability, every available signal points to an easy Barragán re-election.
model.watch: The outlook would shift only in the event of an unforeseen incumbent controversy or a wave of late outside spending against Barragán, neither of which is currently in evidence.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
CA-44 is a heavily Democratic Los Angeles-area seat where Nanette Barragán is seeking another term. The district's roughly twenty-point Democratic lean, combined with her incumbency, gives her a structural advantage that Republican challenger Genevieve Angel has done little to erode. Barragán has raised about $1 million and holds more than $1.1 million on hand, while Angel has raised roughly $22,000, leaving the Republican without resources for a serious television or mail campaign. Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability near 97 percent.

No public general-election polling or expert ratings exist for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and campaign finance. The measurable evidence points uniformly in one direction, and the realistic open question is the size of Barragán's winning margin rather than the outcome itself.
